clinical.summary: 52-year-old male with right above-knee amputation and HIV on BIKTARVY was admitted 7/7/2026 to Providence Little Company of Mary Medical Center San Pedro with one week of progressive right groin pain, redness, swelling and purulent drainage at the prosthesis contact site. CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast (7/7/2026) showed soft tissue edema/skin thickening compatible with cellulitis with suspected ulceration, no abscess or soft tissue gas. He was treated with IV cefTRIAXone and vancomycin, transitioned to oral linezolid (ZYVOX) 600 mg every 12 hours at discharge, and received daily wound care (normal saline cleansing, collagenase/SANTYL, saline-moistened gauze, Mepilex) for a right groin unstageable pressure injury (12 x 1 x 2 cm, 25% yellow slough, moderate serosanguinous drainage). General surgery (Dr. Ginsburg) recommended no surgical debridement and prosthesis use was held. Physical therapy provided wheelchair training. He was discharged 7/11/2026 in stable, improved condition to a recuperative care facility (handwritten face-sheet annotation: Golden State Recuperative Care, 153 E 110th St, Los Angeles 90061). An Outpatient Referral to Home Health was electronically signed 7/10/2026 by Rudo Benjamin, MD requesting skilled nursing (home safety evaluation and needs assessment, assess/instruct wound care/incision care, assess/instruct disease) and physical therapy (mobility, home safety/fall prevention, durable medical equipment needs and training/caregiver training). Face-to-face encounter 7/10/2026; patient certified homebound because of unhealed wounds, need for assistance of another individual, and high fall risk due to gait instability and muscle weakness. Primary diagnosis for home health documented as wound cellulitis. No receiving home health agency is named (Referred To: Not Available; status Pending Review).
